title: PO Boxes, private mailboxes and street addressing

sources.claim: At participating Post Offices, the PO Box "Street Addressing" option lets a box holder use the Post Office street address with the box number, so private carriers that need a street address can deliver; availability varies by location and the customer signs an agreement.

A private mailbox at a Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA) requires USPS Form 1583 and identity documents so the agency may receive mail for the customer. Requirements (for example notarization) have changed; check the current form and the provider.

sections.skill: Compare PO Boxes, private mailboxes and PO Box street addressing

questions.prompt: Where is a PO Box rented?

choices.text: At a Post Office
At the state business filing office
At any coffee shop that sells stamps

questions.correct_answer: At a Post Office
questions.intro: A PO BOX is a locked mailbox rented at a Post Office. Some carriers (like private package companies) need a street address. At participating Post Offices, the "Street Addressing" option lets a box holder use the Post Office's street address with the box number, so those carriers can deliver; availability varies and the customer signs an agreement. A PRIVATE MAILBOX is rented from a private store called a Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA). To receive mail there, the customer completes USPS Form 1583 with identity documents; requirements have changed over time, so check the current form.
questions.feedback: PO Boxes are rented from the Postal Service.

questions.intro: Think of renting a locker at a gym. A PO Box is like a locker at the post office: you get a key and your mail waits there. A private mailbox is like a locker at a private shop that holds mail for you, and you sign a form so the shop may accept your mail. Some delivery companies only drop off at a street address, so some post offices let you write their street address plus your locker number.
